# Add atomic drag execution to the Neural Link client

## Context

A live Neural Link attempt to exercise a Neo splitter exposed a tooling gap: the raw event channel can dispatch the necessary mouse events, but the caller must reconstruct Neo's complete drag-arming recipe and cannot tell whether the gesture actually armed.

Live source verification on Engine `dev` found:

- `src/ai/client/InteractionService.mjs#simulateEvent()` preserves event order and delays, but discards every Boolean returned by `dispatch()` and returns `true` after the loop.
- `src/main/addon/EventSimulator.mjs#dispatch()` returns `false` when the DOM target is absent or event construction/dispatch fails.
- `src/main/draggable/sensor/Mouse.mjs` owns the physical gesture contract: the live delay and minimum-distance thresholds, `drag:start`, `drag:move`, `drag:end`, and lost-release cleanup.
- Four tracked Engine consumers currently spell out `mousedown` / delayed `mousemove` / `mouseup` recipes themselves: Workstation, the cross-window dashboard example, and two whitebox journeys.

The history is consistent. [Engine issue 12884](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/12884) explicitly left a `simulateDrag` convenience primitive out of scope. [Engine issue 12807](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/12807) established the raw Mouse-sensor recipe without adding that primitive. [Engine issue 14772](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/14772) later proved a real cross-window gesture through `simulateEvent`, but embedded the choreography in a product consumer. [Engine issue 16365](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/16365) demonstrated why event arrival is not equivalent to an armed drag.

## The Problem

`simulate_event` is a useful low-level escape hatch, not a gesture transaction:

1. callers duplicate sensor timing, movement thresholds, coordinate conversion, and cleanup;
2. a successful RPC can mean only that the loop completed—even when one event returned `false`;
3. dispatch success does not prove that Neo emitted `drag:start`, processed movement, or reached `drag:end`;
4. putting those browser and sensor semantics into the Brain-side MCP service would reverse the repository boundary and make the server duplicate Engine truth.

The missing Engine capability is one atomic, truthful drag execution primitive that the Brain can expose without knowing DOM or sensor internals.

## The Architectural Reality

- Engine owns both execution realms, with a strict split inside the Body: App-worker `InteractionService` owns JSON-contract validation plus live cross-window geometry; source-window Main `EventSimulator` owns the one atomic native transaction.
- Every synthetic event dispatches in the **source Main realm**. Destination/waypoint windows provide geometry only. App resolves target-local BCR anchors through each target window, converts them to global screen points through `WindowManager.innerRect`, then derives the source-event `clientX/Y` separately.
- `DragDrop` already creates the one live Mouse sensor per Main realm but discards its handle. It must retain/expose that exact instance so execution reads current per-instance `delay` / `minDistance` values; class defaults are not runtime authority.
- Mouse remains the gesture state machine. The executor drives `mousedown` / `mousemove` / `mouseup`; it never calls `startDrag()` or `endGesture()` on the success path.
- Lifecycle proof belongs in source Main: document listeners correlate `drag:start`, `drag:move`, and `drag:end` to the exact native MouseEvent objects constructed by this transaction. Counting an unrelated concurrent drag is forbidden.
- The JSON-RPC contract returns a typed success/failure **result envelope**. Current Engine and Brain error paths discard custom error data, so a thrown Error cannot honestly carry a partial receipt. Brain #204 owns conversion of `success:false` into an MCP tool error.
- Existing `simulate_event` remains the raw escape hatch. It executes the full caller-supplied sequence and accumulates dispatch success; it must never return early and skip a later cleanup event.
- No new production `.mjs` placement is required: extend the existing Client, InteractionService, EventSimulator, DragDrop, and existing test surfaces.

## The Fix

Add `InteractionService#driveDrag()`, register Engine RPC `drive_drag`, and extend the existing Main-thread owners without creating a second drag engine.

The request is JSON-first:

```js
{
    source: {
        targetId: 'required DOM id',
        windowId: 'required source window id',
        anchor  : {x: 0.5, y: 0.5} // optional normalized point, each axis in [0,1]
    },
    destination: {
        // Exactly one mode:
        targetId: 'target DOM id', windowId: 'target window id', anchor: {x: 0.5, y: 0.5}
        // OR target-local point; screen coordinates are derived, never caller-competed:
        windowId: 'target window id', clientX: 240, clientY: 180
        // OR source-relative delta:
        deltaX: 120, deltaY: 0
    },
    waypoints : [], // optional node or target-local point descriptors; no delta waypoints
    steps     : 8,  // post-arm traversal moves across the WHOLE polyline; integer 1..120
    durationMs: 160 // post-arm traversal duration; >= steps * 16 and <= 30000
}
```

When `durationMs` is omitted, Engine derives `max(160, steps * 20)`. This duration begins **after** arming. Source Main always waits the live Mouse-sensor delay, then dispatches one separate arming move beyond the live minimum distance. The requested path must itself reach that threshold; a short path fails at `arming` rather than silently overshooting into another drop zone. The threshold-crossing move emits `drag:start`; `steps` counts later post-arm moves, so at least one observed `drag:move` remains possible.

InteractionService resolves every node/point immediately before the call:

1. node anchors use `DomAccess#getBoundingClientRect` in that node's own window;
2. target-local client coordinates plus that window's live `innerRect` produce the canonical screen point;
3. screen point minus the source window's `innerRect` produces the MouseEvent's source-realm `clientX/Y`;
4. absent live windows, inner rects, zero/non-finite BCRs, ambiguous modes, and inconsistent values fail at `resolution`.

It then sends **one** remote `EventSimulator.driveDrag()` call to `source.windowId`. Mousedown targets the source node. Every later move, terminal up, and best-effort cleanup up dispatches on `document.body` in the source window so source-node replacement cannot strand the Mouse sensor.

Main refuses a second executor while one transaction is active or the live Mouse sensor is already engaged. It correlates lifecycle events by `event.detail.originalEvent` identity against the native events this transaction constructed.

Every RPC returns one envelope. Success:

```js
{
    success: true,
    phase  : 'complete',
    sensor : {delayMs, minDistance},
    dispatch: {down: true, moveCount: 9, up: true},
    observed: {started: true, moveCount: 8, ended: true},
    released: true, // means correlated drag:end observed
    cleanup : {attempted: false, succeeded: true},
    source,
    destination
}
```

Failure returns the same receipt fields with `success:false`, one exact phase
(`resolution|busy|arming|dispatch|movement|release|cleanup`), and
`error:{code,message}`. `dispatch.moveCount` counts raw synthetic moves; `observed.moveCount`
counts correlated `drag:move` lifecycle events. Cleanup cannot turn a failed phase into green.

`simulateEvent()` keeps its Boolean API but executes every event in order, including delays and cleanup events, and returns `true` only when every delegated dispatch returned true.

The Engine test fixture gains a test-only `app.driveDrag(request)` wrapper which calls the raw Engine RPC through the existing Neural Link connection. It does not wait for Brain #204's public MCP service. The public Whitebox E2E guide gains the narrow distinction: `simulateEvent` remains raw sequence control, `driveDrag` owns complete atomic gestures, and `page.mouse` remains the right tool when a test must hold or intervene mid-gesture.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0020 §3` — Neural Link remains the Brain/Body bridge; browser interaction semantics stay Engine-side.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `drive_drag` is registered in the Engine client and accepts the exact source plus discriminated node / target-local-point / source-delta contract above; anchors, bounds, finite coordinates, and one-mode-only rules fail closed.
- [ ] InteractionService resolves BCR/window geometry immediately before execution, derives target-local → screen → source-event coordinates, and sends one atomic call to source Main. Destination window ids never route events.
- [ ] DragDrop retains/exposes the exact live Mouse sensor instance; the executor reads its current delay/minDistance, and a changed-threshold positive control proves no copied literals.
- [ ] Source Main dispatches mousedown on the source node, a separate live-threshold arming move, all post-arm moves and release on document.body, with steps total across the whole polyline and duration applying only post-arm.
- [ ] Success requires correlated `drag:start`, at least one correlated `drag:move`, and correlated `drag:end`; unrelated document drags cannot satisfy the receipt.
- [ ] Receipt separates raw dispatch counts from observed lifecycle counts, includes live sensor values and resolved coordinate spaces, and claims no splitter/grid/dock semantic result.
- [ ] Missing target/geometry, busy sensor, short path, failed dispatch, never-armed sensor, absent move, missing terminal, or failed cleanup returns `success:false` with the exact phase, partial receipt, and cleanup status.
- [ ] A source node removed after arming does not block later moves/release because the stable document-body carrier owns them.
- [ ] `simulateEvent()` preserves its Boolean surface, runs the full supplied sequence, and returns false when any dispatch failed; a mixed-success test proves a later mouseup still runs.
- [ ] Focused units cover request modes/geometry, sensor authority, lifecycle correlation, concurrency, path scheduling, cleanup, and Client routing.
- [ ] The Engine whitebox fixture exposes raw `app.driveDrag(request)` routing without depending on Brain #204 or duplicating the gesture recipe.
- [ ] A live same-window Splitter witness proves physical actuation and a separate width/commit postcondition; a two-window Neural Link witness proves target-local → screen → source-event coordinate routing without coupling to dock-transfer semantics.
- [ ] `learn/guides/testing/WhiteboxE2E.md` documents `simulateEvent` (raw), `driveDrag` (whole atomic gesture), and `page.mouse` (held/mid-gesture intervention) without claiming one replaces the others.
- [ ] Brain #204 remains blocked until this Engine contract merges; it consumes the typed failure envelope and owns MCP error conversion.

## Out of Scope

- The Brain MCP/OpenAPI tool; that is a separate `neo-agent-brain` ticket blocked on this Engine capability.
- DockLayouts architecture, reducer changes, splitter feature work, grid behavior, or any semantic drag outcome.
- Migrating every existing manual recipe in the same PR; one reference witness is enough. Follow-up consumer cleanup must be independently justified.
- Touch/pen gestures, arbitrary pointer-device abstraction, replay ledgers, new diagnostics, or a second drag engine.
- Removing or deprecating `simulate_event`.

## Avoided Traps

- **App-worker event loop called atomic:** rejected; App resolves geometry, source Main executes/observes the one transaction.
- **Destination-window dispatch:** rejected; the source Mouse sensor owns the whole gesture. Destination windows are geometry authorities only.
- **Competing client/screen inputs:** rejected; target-local coordinates derive one screen point and one source-event client point.
- **Brain-side timing constants:** rejected; the retained live Mouse instance owns arming thresholds.
- **Arming move counted as drag:move:** rejected; threshold crossing installs the move listener only afterward.
- **Fail-fast simulateEvent:** rejected; it can skip a caller-supplied mouseup and wedge the sensor.
- **Thrown custom Error receipt:** rejected; current cross-worker/JSON-RPC layers drop custom data. Engine returns a typed failure envelope; Brain converts it.
- **Semantic-operation substitution:** rejected because reducers cannot falsify pointer arming, movement, hit-testing, or release.
- **Bulk caller refactor:** rejected to keep this one Engine primitive and one reference witness.
